title: I own five properties on RM7,000 a month. Am I over-geared?
videoTitle: ASKING SEAN #229 | OWNING 5 PROPERTIES WITH RM 7000 SALARY?
excerpt: A single 36-year-old on RM7,000 a month owns five properties and wants a sixth. Sean thinks he is over-geared: fund what's already due, stress-test vacancies, then buy for quality, not count.

qa.asker: Mr T, a viewer who wrote in by email
qa.context: Mr T, 36, is single, works in banking on a fixed salary of about RM7,000 a month net, and has no debts besides property. He owns five: a terrace house his parents paid for, a service apartment he lives in, a Soho in PJ due for handover soon, and two service apartments under construction bought at 70% loans near MRT stations. A RM82,000 down payment differential on the newest is still to be billed. He has about RM160,000 in money market funds and investments, full insurance, and wants one or two more before 40 to build retirement income.
qa.question: Is he over-geared, should he diversify, and should he buy a sixth property, perhaps a SOFO or SOHO with an 85% loan?
qa.quote: Slow down a little bit; not stop, but slow down a little bit.
qa.answer: Probably yes. His instalments already take about RM4,700 of his RM7,000, and the RM82,000 differential plus renovations for the new units will use up most of his cash. Fund those first, rent the new units out, and build a buffer before buying a sixth; when he does, look for strong deals and quality, not just another property.

reasons.title: Test for empty units
reasons.body: If two units sat empty for six months, he would need about RM18,000 to keep paying, so Sean suggests a buffer of about RM20,000 on top of his other emergency needs. With only about RM2,000 left each month, vacancies would bite fast.

reasons.title: Cash is about to run out
reasons.body: The RM82,000 differential and about RM18,000 to RM25,000 per unit to furnish compact apartments need over RM100,000, close to everything he has saved. A new unit's rent also only counts towards loans six months after it is let.

reasons.title: His picks are sound
reasons.body: Compact units within walking distance of MRT and LRT stations, with instalments of RM1,000 to RM2,000, are sensible choices as Kuala Lumpur rents rise. Held to 70, four rented units could bring in about RM8,000 a month.

reasons.title: Diversifying within property costs more
reasons.body: Land, factories and shop lots need large down payments and holding power. SOFOs and SOHOs with 85% loans and developer rebates can need only 2% to 3% upfront, which Sean thinks is okay, but quality and price against market value matter more.

actions: Set aside the RM82,000 differential and the renovation budgets for the units coming up before planning a sixth purchase.
Keep a vacancy buffer of about RM20,000, more if your parents may need help in an emergency.
Get the new units rented out and let the rent show in your income records before applying for another loan.
Next time, look at subsale, auction and bulk purchase deals, especially ones with high rebates, rather than only retail launches.
Keep your MRTA or MLTA cover in force, and decide who should inherit the portfolio.
qa.caveat: Sean's view depends on comfort: a single person with insured parents can run a thinner buffer than a parent. If he wants to keep buying, he can, but only once the existing commitments are funded.

sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's full English captions for Asking Sean #229. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased. Figures are as the viewer and Sean stated them in November 2023. Sean also mentions EPF Account 2 withdrawals towards a purchase; EPF account rules have changed since, so check the current rules. Sean works with The Makeover Guys, a renovation company he mentions.
